edition.locus: Documenta Catholica Omnia Canones GR (sources/canones_GR.pdf), p. 1, Canon γ´

source_text: Οὐκ ἰδοὺ Ἄχαρ ὁ τοῦ Ζαρᾶ πλημμελείᾳ ἐπλημμέλησεν ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀναθέματος, καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν συναγωγὴν Ἰσραήλ ἐγενήθη ἡ ὀργή; καὶ εἷς μόνος οὗτος ἥμαρτε, μὴ μόνος ἀπέθανεν ἐν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ αὐτοῦ; Ἡμῖν δὲ πᾶν τὸ μὴ ἡμέτερον, ἀλλὰ ἀλλότριον τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ κέρδος, ἀνάθεμα νενομίσθαι προσήκει. Κἀκεῖνος μὲν γὰρ ὁ Ἄχαρ, ἐκ τῆς προνομῆς ἔλαβε· καὶ αὐτοὶ νῦν ἐκ προνομῆς. Κἀκεῖνος μὲν τὰ τῶν πολεμίων· οἱ δὲ νῦν τὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν, κερδάναντες ὀλέθριον κέρδος.
thought_title: Worse than the sin of Achan
orientation: Gregory compares such profiteers with Achan, who took from the devoted spoil of enemies, and judges them worse, since they take what belongs to their brothers.
pass_a_gloss: Not, behold, Achar the [son] of Zara trespassed with a trespass from the devoted thing, and on all the congregation of Israel came wrath? And this one alone sinned; did [he] alone die in his sin? But for us every gain at this time [that is] not ours but another's it is fitting to have been considered a devoted thing. For that Achar took from the plunder; and these too now from plunder. And he [took] the things of the enemies; but these now the things of the brothers, having gained a deadly gain.

choices.english: what was under the ban / a thing under the ban
choices.why: Rendered the same both times so that Gregory's application of Joshua's word to present gain stays visible.
The cognate dative is emphatic; 'grave' carries the emphasis.
The LXX spelling Achar is given in the usual English Bible form.

bible_refs.note: Οὐκ ἰδοὺ Ἄχαρ ὁ τοῦ Ζαρᾶ ... μὴ μόνος ἀπέθανεν, LXX almost word for word; the story itself is Joshua 7

pass_b_english: “Did not Achan son of Zerah commit a grave trespass concerning what was under the ban, and wrath fell on the whole congregation of Israel? He was only one man who sinned; did he die alone in his sin?” (Joshua 22:20). For us, at this time, every gain that is not our own but someone else’s ought to be counted as a thing under the ban. For Achan took from the spoil, and these men too now take from the spoil. But he took what belonged to enemies; these men now take what belongs to their brothers, and reap a deadly gain.
notes: Rubric left out (editorial). The two opening questions quote Joshua 22:20 LXX almost word for word; the story itself is Joshua 7. LXX 'Achar son of Zara' given in the usual English Bible form 'Achan son of Zerah'. ἀνάθεμα rendered 'what was under the ban' / 'a thing under the ban' in both places so that Gregory's application of the word to present gain stays visible. The second question (μὴ μόνος ἀπέθανεν) expects the answer no. πλημμελείᾳ ἐπλημμέλησεν (cognate emphasis) rendered 'commit a grave trespass'.
